memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant of the Lord and have seven priests carry trumpets in front of it." And he ordered the army, "Advance! March around the city, with an armed guard going ahead of the ark of the Lord." — Josh 6:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua wastes no time. As soon as God gives the plan, Joshua passes it on and gets the people moving. He does not debate the strategy or water it down to something that makes more military sense. He simply relays God's word and calls the people to obey. This is the mark of a faithful leader: he does not improve on God's instructions; he delivers them.

Notice the central place of the ark. The ark of the covenant, the symbol of God's presence, was to be carried right into the heart of the procession. This was not merely an army marching; it was a people marching with God in their midst. The whole strange plan made sense only because God's presence was at the centre of it. Take away the ark, and it is just people walking in circles. With the ark, it is the presence of God going out to war.

There is a lesson here for us. Whatever God calls us to do, His presence must be at the centre of it. Our efforts, however sincere, are just "walking in circles" unless God is in the midst of them.

For the believer, God's presence is no longer symbolised by a wooden ark. Christ Himself is Immanuel, God with us (Matt 1:23), and by His Spirit He dwells among His people. As we go out to face our challenges, we do not go alone. We advance with the living presence of God at the very centre of our lives.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to "improve on" God's instructions, or simply obey them?
2. Is God's presence truly at the centre of what you are doing, or off to the side?
3. How does knowing Christ is with you change the way you face your tasks?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me deliver and obey Your word without watering it down. Keep Your presence at the very centre of everything I do. Amen.
